**ABSTRACT:**  
Four mathematical models were examined for predicting bacterial growth. This project aims to estimate the parameters used for different models and select the best fit based on the value of the root mean square error and the coefficient of determination. The goal, as mentioned earlier, is done by using an iteration method, that is, the Gauss-Newton method in Python 3 and was compared with the results provided in the literature by solving with the Gauss-Newton method in MATLAB version 7.11.0.

1. **SUMMARY AND OBJECTIVES:**

This project includes the study of the relationship between the substrate and the growth rate for Escherichia Coli organisms by using four different models: the Blackman model, Monod model, Moser model, and Powell model. 

An iteration method was applied to find the parameters of the models mentioned above, and the best fit was predicted. The root mean square error and the coefficient of determination was measured to find the best fit. The closest value of the coefficient of determination to 1 and the least error is chosen as the best model.

To estimate the parameter's value, the Gauss-Newton method was used, which was applied in the same manner as the literature. The following results are compared with the results from the literature . Additionally, the graphs are plotted to witness the best fit for empirical experimental data.

2. **INTRODUCTION:**

The relationship between the substrate concentration and the microorganisms of different kinds can be acknowledged with the help of microbial growth kinetics \[1\]. The microbes, especially the bacteria, are noticed to grow on variable growth substrates. Substrates are generally the nutrients that are required for the growth of microbial cells. Depending on the type of nutrients, the substrate and the bacteria are cultured \[2\]. In general, it is challenging to generate a relationship between the substrate concentration and the growth rate as the growth rate becomes dependent on the substrate concentration only when the microbes consume the maximum amount of the substrate, leaving no chance of quantifying the growth rate at any level of the substrate concentration \[3\]. 

To overcome the above problem, the first model, Blackman, was proposed in 1905, suggesting that the growth rate is proportional to the substrate concentration at a low substrate concentration. In contrast, the same cannot be said when the concentration of the substrate is increased. The drawback with the model is that when the substrate concentration surpasses the half-saturation coefficient, which is the half value of the maximum growth rate (µm/2), there is a sharp transition from the first order to zero order. However, from zero order to first order, there is no sharp transition to be noticed, so a smooth curve of the function cannot be obtained \[4\]. 

Later, the Monod model noticed the non-linear relationship between the specific growth rate and the limited substrate concentration and formulated the equation for bacterial growth \[3\]. Since the relationship between the growth rate and the substrate concentration is too complex to define, several more modifications were made to establish new models. The major drawback of the Monod model is that it does not account for the products produced when the cells do not grow \[4\]. Moser upgraded the Monod model with an extra adjustable parameter, n. Later, the Powell model got introduced by modifying the Moser model by introducing a maintenance rate.

3. **METHODOLOGY:**

**3.1 EXPERIMENTAL DATA**  
At low feed rates, a continuous flow of the feed solution is set up in the reaction chamber with a constant culture volume \[3\]. The data set was obtained for the original culture of E. coli by maintaining the continuous flow and varying the feed rate. The data set provided in the reference paper has the wrong units, therefore updating the data set with the correct units. The data set consists of bacterial growth rate (m) and the concentration of the substrate (s) \[3\].

**3.2 MODEL DEVELOPMENT:**  
The generalized form of the nonlinear growth models for the Blackman, Monod, Moser, and Powell models can be inscribed as:

μi \= f(si , **B**) \+ εi,  
Where i range from 1 to n where n is the number of data sets, and in this case, it is 15, m and s are the response and the independent variable, respectively. **B **is defined as the vector of parameters. εi is the random error in the model \[4\].

The Blackman model can be described with the following equation, where μ is the growth rate of the cell, μm is the maximum specific growth rate, s is the substrate concentration and ks is the half- saturation constant. 

μ \= $\{\frac{m*s}{ks}\ \ \ \ if\ s<ks\ m\ \ \ \ \ if\ s≥ks{\ }$

Monod model is described as,

μ \= ((μm \* s))/( ks \+ s))

In this case, s being the concentration of the nutrient at time t and μ is the specific growth rate. μ is the function of s and so it will increase sharply for low level of substrate concentration and for high level of the substrate concentration it increases slowly until a saturation of the bacteria is reached.  
The Moser model is described as,

μ \= (μm \* sn)/( ks \+ sn)  
Where n is defined as an adjustable parameter and so it provides the degree of flexibility in fitting the data.  
The Powell model is defined as,  
μ \= ((μm \+ m) \* s)/(ks \+ s) – m  
where m is the maintenance rate.

**3.3 DETERMINATION OF MODEL PARAMETERS:**  
Out of the four models, Blackman and Monod's model has two parameters to find, and Moser and Powell have three parameters to be estimated. The parameters were determined by using the Gauss-Newton approximation. It is defined by minimizing the sum of the square residual. The key point in estimating the parameters from this method is to have a good initial parameter value as the model equations are nonlinear. As a result, the convergence will be slow, and the estimated parameters obtained may not be reliable. For this method, the first-order partial derivatives are only considered, and the elements in the jacobian reflect local properties. The partial derivatives are with respect to each parameter \[4\] in the specified model. The parameters are approximated with successive iterations from the provided computational method.

**3.4 INITIAL VALUE SPECIFICATION:**  
To have faster convergence with the fitted value, a good approximation of the initial values is required. The initial values of the four parameters used in the above-mentioned models can be estimated in the following way:  
Initial value of μm for all four models – It is defined as the maximum value of μ in the data set.   
So, μm \= 0.852

Initial value of ks for all four models – It is defined as the half- saturation constant \[4\] .  
μ \= μm/2 where s \= ks  
So, ks \= 58

Initial value of n for the Moser model – It is defined with the following expression:

n \= (log(μ0  \* ks0)/( μm0 \- μ0))/log(s0)  
So, n \= 0.897

Initial value of m for the Powell model – It is defined with the following expression:

m \= (μm0 \* s0 \- μ0 \* ks0 \- μm0 \* s0)/( ks0)  
So, m \= 0.059

**3.5 BEST FIT:**  
The coefficient of data R2 is determined to select the best fit. The model with the R2 value closest to one is selected. It is done so without using the package. Also, a comparison of the models with the best fit is presented.

4. **RESULTS AND DISCUSSIONS:**

To validate the results obtained in the literature, the Gauss-Newton method is applied without using the solver in Python 3\. The R2 values in Table 2, when solved via the computational method, shows that the model closest to 1 is the Moser model, and so it should be the best fit for the given empirical experimental data, and as per the literature, the Moser model is the best fit. There has been a slight variation in the values for the RMSE (root mean square error), R2 (coefficient of determination) and the parameters( µm, ks, n and m). The major difference between the values estimated and provided in the literature can be pointed out for the Blackman model, but it is a bad fit in the literature and as well as when being computed again. The variation in the values can be because the random error was not considered while programming or the data set was not up to the proper decimal points. There might be a variation in calculating the initial values, which is the critical point in estimating the parameters as there was no proper value specified in the literature, and it only is explained via theory or expression. There is also a possibility of some error in the paper, as pointed out earlier, since the curve obtained for the Blackman model is how it should be, and as mentioned before, modifications were made to upgrade the Blackman model since it does not provide a smooth curve. 

5. **CONCLUSION:**

The focus of this project is to find the best fit for the empirical experimental data of E.coli growth rate by estimating the parameters using Gauss-Newton iteration. It is found that the best fit is the Moser model having the least RMSE and high R2, much closer to 1\. The Moser model and Powell model are also a good fit for the given empirical data. Also, Gauss-Newton proves to be a good source to estimate the parameters for the kinetic models for microbial growth rate, which will help in future research when the more complex system will be studied, such as industrial–domestic waste treatment, recycling processes, sewage treatment, etc. clean-up strategies \[2\].
